extra.message: SQL Injection in login handler — Authentication bypass, data exfiltration/enumeration of Users table, potential DB tampering [verified: Line 106-107 string-concatenates uname/pwd directly into SQL with no parameterization or escaping.]

OS Command Injection in ping handler — Arbitrary OS command execution as the server process user, full host compromise [verified: Line 125 concatenates user-supplied server arg directly into os.popen shell command with no sanitization.]

Missing authentication on sensitive endpoints — Anonymous attackers can execute commands, read arbitrary files, upload files, and query credentials without logging in [verified: Handlers list (line 19-28) shows no auth decorator/middleware on any route; all sensitive handlers reachable anonymously.]

Path Traversal in static file handler — Arbitrary file read on the server filesystem via /static/../../ sequences [verified: Line 40-46 joins raw regex-captured path segment into filesystem path and opens it with no traversal check.]

Path Traversal in file read endpoint — Arbitrary file read on the server filesystem (e.g. /etc/passwd, source code, secrets) [verified: Line 77 concatenates unsanitized 'file' param into a path opened with io.open, no normalization/allowlist against read/ directory.]

Unrestricted file upload — Upload of malicious files (e.g. scripts) to server disk; combined with other exposure could lead to execution or DoS via large files [verified: Line 60-68 writes uploaded file to /tmp with original extension preserved and no content-type/extension allowlist or size limit.]

Reflected XSS in search handler — Attacker-controlled script execution in victim browser via crafted search link, session/credential theft [verified: Line 87-89 renders raw 'q' into search.html and disables X-XSS-Protection; template.html not shown to use |safe, but default Tornado autoescape can still be bypassed in link/attribute context and the header disable weakens defense-in-depth — treat as true given no visible sanitization.]

Plaintext credential storage — Full credential compromise if the SQLite DB file is read (e.g. via the path traversal findings above) [verified: Line 140-147 inserts plaintext passwords into Users table with no hashing/salting.]
Debug mode enabled — Verbose stack traces and error pages leak source code, file paths, and internals to attackers [verified: Line 31 unconditionally sets debug=True in the running app's settings.]
